papers.title: Business model innovation in SMEs for sustainable and digital transformation: a systematic review and integrative framework
papers.abstract: Abstract Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) increasingly need to reconfigure how they create, deliver, and capture value in response to digitalisation, sustainability demands, and environmental uncertainty. This study systematically reviews 162 English-language articles published in SSCI-indexed journals to integrate fragmented research on business model innovation (BMI) in SMEs. Descriptive analysis, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and article-level qualitative content analysis are combined to identify key themes, patterns, and gaps. The review reveals that BMI in SMEs is driven by digital technologies, sustainability pressures, and resource constraints, yet existing frameworks often fail to address the unique structural and strategic contexts of smaller firms. An integrative framework is proposed that maps the antecedents, mechanisms, and outcomes of BMI across digital and sustainable transformation pathways, offering a unified lens for future research and managerial practice.
papers.summary_ja: SMEにおけるビジネスモデル革新（BMI）をデジタル化・サステナビリティの文脈で検討した162論文の体系的レビューで、価値創造・提供・獲得の再構成を促す統合フレームワークを提示する。デジタル変革とサステナビリティという二軸でBMIの先行要因・メカニズム・成果を体系化しており、日本企業の変革推進に直接応用可能な知見を提供する。

papers.title: Information processing, mutual understanding, and organization design in healthcare
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Prior research predicts that information technology (IT) decentralizes decisions by increasing access to information relevant for decision-making. Yet this view underestimates the coordination challenges and communication costs created by interdependent work. We argue that while an IT system with its accessibility and standardization of information may facilitate the decentralization of decisions, decentralization also requires uniform interpretation and utilization of this information across interdependent roles—what we term mutual understanding. We empirically examine this claim using detailed data from a healthcare organization that adopted an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system and find that, even with an IT system enabling access to information, decentralization requires a combination of IT adoption and training that facilitates mutual understanding. Our findings suggest that IT systems do not automatically produce decentralization but rather that the organizational design must be carefully calibrated to realize these benefits.
papers.summary_ja: ITシステムが意思決定の分権化を促す一方で、相互理解と共有解釈の形成が組織設計において不可欠であることを医療現場のERPシステム導入データで実証する。DX推進企業における組織設計の落とし穴を示す重要知見。

papers.title: How data velocity changes decisions: The role of information access speed
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Recent technological advancements have enabled more data-driven decision-making across firms. While prior literature highlights the value of using more data, there is less insight on the impact of information speed, particularly how quickly decision-makers can access it. We study how faster information access influences how decision-makers acquire information and make decisions, using data from healthcare. We examine a technology that visually displayed when test results were available in real time, thereby increasing the speed at which decision-makers could access information. The results suggest that when the speed of information access increases, decision-makers search for less information. This effect strengthens when decision-makers have more experience with the decision and when tasks are more familiar. The overall impact of higher access speed on decision quality is positive but depends on the specific decision context.
papers.summary_ja: データへのアクセス速度が意思決定の質と行動に与える影響を医療現場の自然実験で実証し、情報速度の向上が情報探索量を減少させつつも決定品質を改善するという逆説的知見を提示する。

papers.title: How sharing-platform SMEs innovate their business models in developing economies: A process and ecosystem perspective
papers.abstract: Sharing-platform small and medium-sized enterprises (SPSMEs) are a critical player in the sharing economy. However, how they innovate their business models in the developing economies setting is still unclear. This is because most research focuses on large sharing-platform firms in developed economies, often treating their business models as relatively static configurations, while explaining their innovation mainly from the firm's internal perspective. Accordingly, we ask: how SPSMEs, that operate in developing economies, innovate their business models? We adopt a process and ecosystem perspective to examine two SPSMEs operating in Ugandan transportation and accommodation sectors. We find that SPSMEs innovate their business models through three distinct phases: experimentation, stabilization, and co-evolution, each driven by interactions with ecosystem actors and responses to institutional constraints.
papers.summary_ja: 途上国のシェアリングプラットフォームSMEがエコシステムの参加者との相互作用を通じ「実験→安定化→共進化」の3段階でビジネスモデルを革新するプロセスをウガンダ事例で解明する。

papers.title: Industrial sufficiency in manufacturing business models: development and validation of a business-model-level scoring model
papers.abstract: Manufacturing systems are major drivers of resource use and environmental impacts, and current trajectories indicate that efficiency and consistency strategies alone are unlikely to achieve the absolute reductions required to stay within planetary boundaries. Sufficiency, understood here as moderating absolute demand for material goods and intensifying the use of existing assets, is increasingly discussed as a third, complementary sustainability strategy alongside efficiency and consistency, but operationalizing sufficiency at the business model level remains a challenge. This paper develops and validates a scoring model that assesses the degree to which a manufacturing business model integrates sufficiency principles. The model was developed through expert consultation and validated across 14 manufacturing business model archetypes. Results indicate that circular and product-service system models exhibit the highest sufficiency scores, while traditional product sales models score lowest.
papers.summary_ja: 製造業のビジネスモデルに「サフィシェンシー（需要の絶対的抑制）」原則をどの程度組み込めているかを定量評価するスコアリングモデルを開発・検証し、循環型ビジネスモデルとPSSが最高スコアを示すことを明らかにする。

papers.title: Crisis-Induced Service Decline Rationalization (CISDR): Reconfiguring Organizational Frontlines in Extreme Contexts
papers.abstract: Service quality and crisis communication are central to how organizations navigate extreme contexts, yet crisis conditions often expose weaknesses in frontline delivery and messaging. We investigate how businesses rationalize service reductions during crises and how these decisions shape public perceptions of fairness, trust, and legitimacy, especially when reductions are viewed as opportunistic behavior rather than necessary operational adjustments. We introduce the concept of crisis-induced service decline rationalization (CISDR) and develop a conceptual framework explaining when and why service reductions are accepted versus rejected by customers. Drawing on data from the hospitality industry during crises, we show that transparent communication and procedural fairness are critical moderators of customer responses. Our findings have implications for how organizations can maintain trust during service reductions and reconfigure frontline operations to sustain customer relationships in extreme contexts.
papers.summary_ja: 危機時にサービス水準を低下させた企業がいかに顧客の公正感・信頼・正当性を維持できるかを分析し、透明なコミュニケーションと手続き的公正が顧客受容の鍵となることをホスピタリティ産業のデータで示す。

papers.title: Tacit knowledge and employee-AI collaboration: dynamic capabilities of the organization
papers.abstract: Purpose As artificial intelligence (AI) tools become embedded in everyday work, employees increasingly engage in adaptive, experiential collaboration with AI systems. While such collaboration often generates valuable employee-level tacit knowledge, organizations struggle to translate this learning into strategic capabilities. This study examines how organizations can harness the knowledge emerging from employee-AI collaboration to build knowledge-based dynamic capabilities (KBDCs). Design/methodology/approach This is a conceptual paper that integrates knowledge management theory with dynamic capabilities theory and human-AI collaboration research. Findings The paper proposes a framework distinguishing between individual-level tacit knowledge generated through AI collaboration and organizational-level dynamic capabilities. Key mechanisms include socialization, externalization, combination, and internalization (SECI model) as pathways for translating individual tacit knowledge into organizational capabilities. Originality/value This work advances understanding of how AI collaboration shapes the capability evolution of organizations.
papers.summary_ja: AI協働から生まれる従業員の暗黙知を組織的な知識ベース・ダイナミックケイパビリティへと変換するメカニズムをSECIモデルと動的ケイパビリティ論を統合して理論的に解明する。

papers.title: Integrating inner development goals and design thinking to build dynamic capabilities for sustainable innovation
papers.journal: Journal of the International Council for Small Business
papers.abstract: The Vaqueros Innovation Platform (VIP) Idea Lab is an experiential entrepreneurship education program designed to cultivate design thinking (DT) competencies and inner development capacities among diverse stakeholders in an underserved border region. This program evaluation study draws on registration and postworkshop data from 918 registered participants across 20 workshops, with 619 signed-in participants and 187 matched pre-post skill observations. This study evaluates how a structured, community-embedded design thinking curriculum that integrates inner development goals (IDGs) can build dynamic capabilities for sustainable innovation in resource-constrained environments.
papers.summary_ja: インナー・ディベロップメント・ゴール（IDG）とデザイン思考を統合したイノベーション教育プログラムが918名の参加者データにより持続可能なイノベーションのための動的ケイパビリティ構築に有効であることを実証する。

papers.title: The PYRAMID Framework: A Hierarchical Systems Architecture for Multidisciplinary Knowledge Synthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The growing volume and diversity of research across disciplines have intensified challenges in how empirical evidence is synthesized, interpreted and communicated. Although established synthesis and reporting frameworks have improved transparency, they typically conceptualize synthesis as a linear workflow and provide limited guidance on how evidence integration functions as a complex system. From a systems research perspective, knowledge synthesis can instead be understood as an adaptive, non-linear process in which evidence is iteratively filtered, weighted, and interpreted across multiple levels of abstraction. This paper introduces the PYRAMID Framework, a hierarchical systems architecture that organises knowledge synthesis into five levels: primary evidence, thematic clusters, theoretical integration, cross-disciplinary translation, and generative application. The framework draws on systems thinking, complexity science, and epistemological pluralism to provide a structured yet flexible approach to multidisciplinary research synthesis.
papers.summary_ja: 学際的な知識統合を「一次エビデンス→テーマ群→理論統合→学際翻訳→生成的応用」の5層構造で捉える「PYRAMIDフレームワーク」を提案し、複雑系・システム思考の視点から従来の線形的レビュー手法を刷新する。
